references.text: Describes the place the Lord will choose to put His name, where the Israelites shall bring their offerings and tithes and eat them there.
Prohibits eating the tithe of grain, wine, and oil within the gates, but commands that it be eaten before the Lord at the chosen place.
Concerns the firstborn of cattle and sheep that are to be consecrated to the Lord and eaten before Him at the chosen place.
The purpose of the commandments is to fear the Lord all days, which aligns with the goal of learning to fear the Lord.
A fundamental law regarding the tithe of the land's produce and fruits that belong to the Lord.
The tithe is given to the Levites as their inheritance for service at the tabernacle.
The people commit themselves to bringing the tithe of grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses of the house of the Lord.
To fear the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, which reflects the purpose of the commandment about tithing.
Concerns the place where the Lord causes His name to be remembered and will bless the people.
The Passover sacrifice shall be slaughtered at the place the Lord chooses to put His name there.
